findings.finding: AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore's default version is v2 (created 2019-05-23): three Allow statements on Resource '*' with 15 ssm:, 4 ssmmessages: and 6 ec2messages: actions, 25 in all. These are copied verbatim into the boundary and the supporting-services policy.

In geographic cross-Region inference Bedrock authorises the inference profile (with the source Region), the foundation model in the source Region and the foundation model in each destination Region; for the foundation-model evaluations aws:RequestedRegion is the destination Region and bedrock:InferenceProfileArn is set. An Allow on the routed models conditioned on aws:RequestedRegion = the source Region alone would therefore refuse every routed call. This contradicts the R5 handoff's sections 3 and 4 ('the routed Regions appear as resources, not as requested Regions').
findings.basis: Bedrock user guide 'Geographic cross-Region inference' (an SCP restricting Regions must allow all destination Regions or exempt them by bedrock:InferenceProfileArn; the profile evaluation carries the source Region and no bedrock:InferenceProfileArn); AWS ML blog 2026-01-13 (example policy: models in all destination Regions, conditioned on bedrock:InferenceProfileArn). Corroborated by v1 history: the v1 invoke policy already matched arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-* but carried aws:RequestedRegion in {eu-west-1, us-east-1}, and the call to a profile routing to us-east-2 succeeded only after an unconditioned policy named the us-east-2 model (evidence/02_iam/IAM_Least_Privilege_logs.txt). Not provable by IAM simulation, where the context is supplied by the caller; shown by R11's live call.

findings.finding: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy (properties Description, Groups, ManagedPolicyName, Path, PolicyDocument, Roles, Users; Ref returns the ARN) and AWS::IAM::InstanceProfile (InstanceProfileName, Path, Roles; Ref returns the name, GetAtt Arn) take no Tags. Both join UNTAGGABLE_TYPES in tools/aws_template_guard.py. AWS::IAM::Role takes Tags and carries Name and project.
findings.basis: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-iam-managedpolicy.html and aws-resource-iam-instanceprofile.html, read 2026-10-24 (R5 handoff) and again 2026-10-25; cfn-lint 1.57.2 exit 0 on the filled template.

findings.finding: Before R5 the account holds no customer-managed policy and no instance profile, and no role named proposal-orchestrator-*: thirteen roles, three AWS-managed under /managed/ (AccountFullAccessRole, AWSManagedAccountManagementAccessRole, AWSManagedAdvancedFeaturesActivationRole) and ten AWS service-linked roles under /aws-service-role/. Every fixed name R5 uses is free, and no policy named or described as temporary or validation exists.

The AWS CLI v2 returns exit status 254 when the service answers with an error (here DescribeStacks ValidationError 'Stack with id proposal-orchestrator-iam does not exist'); the step sheet's criterion had said 255. Windows PowerShell also wraps the error text at the console width inside the file. The R5 step 03 criterion is corrected in STEPS.md with a dated note; the evidence is unchanged.

decisions.question: Deploy-bucket prefix for the runtime role (plans/aws_redeployment_r5_handoff_2026-10-24.md section 4, point 1)
decisions.answer: Lasting rule: one prefix, bundles/, read-only for the runtime role. s3:ListBucket on the bucket with Condition StringLike s3:prefix = bundles/*; s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket; s3:GetObject on bundles/*. Bucket name derived as ${ProjectName}-deploy-${AWS::AccountId}. The R4 S3 gateway endpoint policy stays as it is.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '1a'. The narrowest read the AN12 tarball and its .sha256 need (F7).
decisions.consequence: R7's bucket policy and R15's runbook use the same prefix; R15 uploads to bundles/. R7 and R15 inherit this rule.

decisions.question: How S3 appears in the explicit deny (point 2)
decisions.answer: Deny s3:* with NotResource = the deploy bucket and its bundles/* objects. Every other S3 resource is explicitly denied; inside the bucket, writes are implicitly denied (no Allow grants them).
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '2a'. Exit condition 2 asks for an explicit deny of S3 outside the policy, which IAM simulation shows as explicitDeny.
decisions.consequence: Step 09 expects explicitDeny for s3:GetObject on another in-account bucket and implicitDeny for s3:PutObject on bundles/. If R11 shows that Run Command needs the SSM Agent's regional buckets, both R4-D3's endpoint policy and this deny gain a statement by UPDATE change set, with a successor record.

decisions.question: DC-16: where the Region condition lives (point 3), corrected by F-R5-2
decisions.answer: The invoke policy has two statements: (i) the inference-profile ARNs with StringEquals aws:RequestedRegion = ${AWS::Region}; (ii) the foundation-model ARNs with StringEquals bedrock:InferenceProfileArn in InferenceProfileArns and aws:RequestedRegion in RoutedRegions. The explicit deny refuses the two invoke actions when aws:RequestedRegion is not in RoutedRegions (DC-16); this also refuses global. routing, whose Region is 'unspecified'.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '3a' to the agent's corrected proposal. The handoff's proposal (models allowed only for aws:RequestedRegion = eu-north-1) would refuse every routed call (F-R5-2). The bedrock:InferenceProfileArn condition is AWS's recommended pattern and admits the models only through the OD7 profiles.
decisions.consequence: Step 09's allowed foundation-model cases supply two context entries (aws:RequestedRegion = the model's Region, bedrock:InferenceProfileArn = its profile); a model case without the profile context is expected implicitDeny. R11's live call is the proof of F-R5-2; R11's Bedrock endpoint policy must admit the same resources. R12b's DC-17 negative test hits the region deny.

decisions.question: Flow-log group name (point 4)
decisions.answer: Lasting rule: the flow-log group is /${ProjectName}/vpc-flow-logs, ARN arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/${ProjectName}/vpc-flow-logs:*. The flow-logs role may write only there (logs:CreateLogStream, PutLogEvents, DescribeLogGroups, DescribeLogStreams), and its trust policy admits vpc-flow-logs.amazonaws.com only with aws:SourceAccount = ${AWS::AccountId} and aws:SourceArn like arn:${AWS::Partition}:ec2:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:vpc-flow-log/*.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '4a'. R5's role and R6's key policy must scope to the group R7 creates; the confused-deputy condition is the one the VPC user guide recommends.
decisions.consequence: R7 creates the group under exactly this name; R6 scopes CloudWatch Logs to the prefix /${ProjectName}/.

decisions.question: Names (point 5)
decisions.answer: Fixed names under Path /: ${ProjectName}-runtime-role, -runtime-profile, -boundary, -explicit-deny, -bedrock-invoke, -supporting-services, -deploy-bucket-read, -flow-logs-role, -flow-logs-write. All policies are managed policies; no inline policy.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '5a'. Stable ARNs for R6, R8, R11 and the evidence commands; each policy has an ARN for get-policy-version.
decisions.consequence: The change set needs --capabilities CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM. A name change replaces the resource.

decisions.question: kms:GenerateDataKey* and kms:ViaService (point 6)
decisions.answer: No kms:GenerateDataKey* (the role writes nothing encrypted). The boundary allows kms:Decrypt and kms:DescribeKey on this account's keys in this Region; no identity policy grants them. A kms:ViaService condition, if any, goes into R6's key-policy grant, not into the boundary.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '6a'. One place for the KMS narrowing; the boundary stays simple.
decisions.consequence: R6 decides ViaService in its key policy, built with ${AWS::Region}.
